doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Recording with Hutcherson, 1977
summary: Listening to a 1977 track with Manny Boyd, he recalls Hutcherson's albums being rehearsed and recorded in two days, with Orrin Keepnews producing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I think I have a piece here that you played on.
Oh yeah. We used to play this song a lot. That’s with Manny. Is Manny Boyd on this I think?
What kind of time are you used to, being in a studio to get in album done?

You know in these days when we used to do these albums it would be like — first I would get there and Bobby would have nothing together. And we’d get there and rehearse the tunes and maybe we’d do it like in two days at the most. At the most. It’s unbelievable how fast we used to do those. But we were playing all the time though.
Yeah. I think Orrin Keepnews produced some of this stuff, didn’t he?
